summary: C3 executed successfully (return code 0) as a conditional calculation, not an empirical fit. For alpha=1 and tau=5 h, equal integrated r=1 schedules give x_end=.6321 for fast production (.2 h^-1 for 5 h; threshold .5 crossed at 3.466 h) and .2454 for slow production (.05 h^-1 for 20 h; no crossing). Sensitivity matters: tau=1 h yields no crossing over tested alpha values; tau=20 h with alpha=1 yields crossing in both schedules, at 2.671 h fast and 13.863 h slow. Thus schedule dependence is conditional, not universal. The linear state can exceed 1 (up to 1.77 in the grid), so x must be interpreted as an unbounded dimensionless effective load proxy, not a bounded fraction; a physical bounded-state model would need another constitutive term. Equilibrium alternative predicts schedule-independent endpoint only after matching final composition and equilibration. E2 contains measured reference/variant RNA concentrations (ng/uL) across three tie-line indices: dilute reference 27.48, 53.68, 92.98 and variant 0, .53, 115.63; dense reference 12893, 12805, 48826 and variant 0, 4787, 20352. Reported errors are large in several entries, and conditions/construct mapping to A/B is unknown. E2 shows phase composition varies but cannot be mapped to the phenotype or used to infer kinetic arrest. R3_S3 abstract reports a specific trans RNA-RNA kissing-loop interaction contributing to oskar RNP granule assembly and synergizing with Bruno in Drosophila oocytes and in-vitro assays; it supports RNA-RNA contacts as a possible architectural mechanism but gives no exchange times, transferable concentration, or target-specific arrest. Other R3 hits are design/review papers or riboswitch ligand folding and do not supply target junction kinetics. I issue T4 requests for DNA-only sequence/read-frequency evidence and background on amplification heterogeneity.

hypotheses: H1 (new, unconfirmed): production-driven accumulation of connected RNA loop junctions can outrun relaxation and trap internal solvent-rich domains after an effective-load threshold.

H3 alternative: amplification-linked carryover or imaging/segmentation changes explain some or all of the contrast.

candidates.initial_boundary_conditions: C3 assumes x0=0, r constant within each schedule, no spatial geometry; q is not simulated. General model x(0)>=0 and r>=0. No conservation claim.
candidates.observation_mapping: E0 is segmented dark area / filled area. E1 is aggregate displacement. E2 is measured reference/variant concentration by phase and tie-line index in ng/uL, but no condition or construct mapping to A/B. None directly measures x or establishes that dark area is solvent-rich cavity volume.
alternatives: H2 equilibrium demixing set by final composition/ionic conditions; schedule-independent only after composition matching and adequate equilibration.
H3 amplification carryover changes transcription or optics.
H4 segmentation/tracking selection changes measured observables.
predictions: C3: at alpha=1,tau=5 h, fast equal-dose schedule crosses xc at 3.466 h and ends x=.6321; slow does not cross and ends x=.2454. H1 predicts threshold-state difference; H2 predicts convergence after matched composition and equilibration.
This contrast is parameter conditional: tau=1 h none of the tested alpha values cross; tau=20 h and alpha=1 both schedules cross.
If B crossed threshold by 24 h, the conditional 36/48 h commitment is area B>A with reduced B growth rate, dependent on the uncalibrated area mapping.
checks: C3 returned code 0; every schedule has integrated r=1 and x_end is nonnegative.
Units: alpha*r and x/tau are h^-1; qdot terms h^-1. Closed form is integrating-factor solution; r=0 gives exponential decay.
C3 x exceeds 1 for some settings, so x cannot be treated as a bounded fraction without modifying the model; here it is explicitly an unbounded effective load proxy.
No q prediction is computed; post-threshold freeze stipulates persistence.
E2 errors are large for several entries and metadata is insufficient to map reference/variant to A/B or history; it does not adjudicate H1 versus H2.

R3_S3 supports RNA-RNA contacts in another RNP system but no loop exchange rate, production coupling, or cavity arrest.
E2 is compatible with phase composition differences but lacks A/B identity and causal conditions.
